$comment: Reviewed exceptions to the `npm audit` CI gate. Consumed by scripts/audit-gate.mjs.
This is NOT a way to make CI quiet. The gate still runs at --audit-level=moderate over
ALL dependencies (prod AND dev). Only the exact advisories listed here are subtracted,
and each one must carry a reachability argument and a reviewBy date. Anything new fails.
1. Key on the ROOT advisory (the GHSA that npm audit reports as an object in `via`),
not on the packages that merely depend on it. One root entry clears its whole chain.
2. `reason` must argue REACHABILITY in THIS app, not severity in the abstract.
3. `reviewBy` is a hard deadline. Past it, CI fails until someone re-reviews.
Bumping the date is a decision that needs a human, not a rubber stamp.
4. An entry only belongs here if there is genuinely no forward fix. Check first:
a fix that exists is always preferred over an exception. See LEGACY note in

allow.reason: CSRF bypass confined to React Router's unstable RSC (React Server Components) code paths -- the advisory itself states it 'only affects your application if you are using the unstable RSC APIs'. This app is a client-side Vite SPA: src/main.jsx mounts <BrowserRouter>, all 54 router imports come from 'react-router-dom', and the tree contains zero RSC entrypoints (no unstable_RSC, routeRSCServerRequest, matchRSCServerRequest, createCallServer, or @vitejs/plugin-rsc). There is no server-rendered action pipeline for the bypass to act on.
allow.noFixAvailable: Patched only in react-router 8.3.0. react-router-dom has no 8.x published at all (v8 consolidated the package), and react-router-dom@7.18.1 pins react-router to exactly 7.18.1 -- so react-router cannot be bumped underneath it. The affected range covers every 7.x from 7.12.0 up, including the latest 7.x release (7.18.2, re-checked against the npm registry 2026-08-07), so no upgrade within the 7 line clears it -- do not read a newer 7.x on npm as a fix. Fixing this is NOT an import rename -- do not scope it as one. Every react-router 8.x (8.0.0, 8.1.0, 8.2.0 and the patched 8.3.0) declares peerDependencies react >= 19.2.7 and react-dom >= 19.2.7, verified against the npm registry 2026-08-07. This app is on React 18.3.1, so the advisory is gated behind a React 18 -> 19 MAJOR UPGRADE of the whole frontend, which also pulls @tanstack/react-query, @tanstack/react-table, react-hook-form, @testing-library/react and @vitejs/plugin-react into compatibility review. The v7 -> v8 move itself (54 import sites from 'react-router-dom' to 'react-router', plus v8 breaking changes) is only the last step of that. Budget it as its own project, well before the reviewBy date rather than at it.
allow.clearWhen: The React 18 -> 19 upgrade AND the react-router v7 -> v8 migration both land (in that order -- v8 will not install on React 18), or the v7 line receives a backport of the RSC fix.
